title: Directed winding on toroidal orientations obeys an exact polar duality
subject: Which homology classes the directed closed walks of a toroidal orientation realize, and what the conjectured 3/4 wrapping of strongly-connected percolation means
conclusion: On any square-lattice torus, the primitive classes of an orientation's directed closed walks are exactly those in a closed convex cone, and the rotated dual orientation realizes exactly those in its polar; the uniform orientation's cone has a polar-invariant law. So the conjecture that strongly-connected percolation wraps in one direction with probability 3/4 is equivalent to: with probability 1/4, no directed closed walk winds horizontally.
